rules.title: Portland ban on algorithm-assisted rental price coordination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithm-assisted rental price coordination. Private remedies are available against owners of 16 or more units: the greater of treble damages or $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: Private remedy against owners of 16+ units: greater of treble damages or $1,000 per violation

coverage.landlord_size_condition: Private remedies apply to owners of 16 or more units; the source does not say whether the prohibition itself has a size threshold.
coverage.summary: Prohibits algorithm-assisted rental price coordination in Portland. Private remedies are limited to owners of 16 or more units. The source states no other coverage limits.
coverage.owner_conditions: Owners of 16 or more units (for private remedies)

rules.effective_date_note: The only source gives the effective date as 'February 2026', with no day. The ordinance is in force as of the query date (2026-10-01) either way.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits algorithm-assisted rental price coordination; for owners of 16 or more units, private remedies include the greater of treble damages or $1,000 per violation.
rules.review_note: Supported only by a secondary law-firm summary (Morgan Lewis, Aug. 21, 2026); the ordinance text was not captured. Items to verify against the official Portland City Code: the exact effective date, the ordinance number, the definition of covered software, any coverage threshold for the prohibition itself, and any public enforcement penalties.
